thought_title: He Truly Suffered; They Only Seem

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα ἔπαθεν δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα σωθῶμεν: καὶ ἀληθῶς ἔπαθεν, ὡς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν, οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, αὐτοὶ το δοκεῖν ὄντες: καὶ καθὼς φρονοῦσιν, καὶ συμβήσεται αὐτοῖς, οὖσιν ἀσωμάτοις καὶ δαιμονικοῖς.
pass_a_gloss: [1] For he suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved. And he truly suffered, just as he also truly raised himself, not as some unbelievers say, that he suffered in appearance, while they themselves exist in appearance. And just as they think, so it will also happen to them: they will be without bodies and like demons.

lemmas.gloss: raise up (transitive, here reflexive with ἑαυτόν)

pass_b_english: All of this he suffered for us, so that we might be saved. And he suffered truly, just as he truly raised himself. Some unbelievers say his suffering was only an appearance. No, it is they who are only an appearance! And what they believe will become their lot: they will end up bodiless, like the demons.

choices.term: τὸ δοκεῖν … αὐτοὶ τὸ δοκεῖν ὄντες
choices.english: only an appearance … it is they who are only an appearance
choices.why: Ignatius turns the docetists' slogan back on them; kept as two short blows.
rejected: only seem to be Christians (ANF supplies 'Christians')

choices.why: Active, reflexive: Christ as agent of his own rising; not smoothed into passive.
Two predicates kept; 'like the demons' renders the adjective without inventing 'evil spirits' as a noun class.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF supplies '[Christians]' after 'only seem to be'; the Greek has no noun, so this draft leaves the barb bare.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 2 (sections 1); old ANF span covers the full chapter.
Pack topic: heresy-schism. Same chapter English is shared by every excerpt id on this chapter.
Pack Greek prints 'δἰ' (for δι’) and 'το δοκεῖν' without accent; copied as printed.

review.notes: P1 matches Smyrnaeans 2. «Ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα ἔπαθεν δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα σωθῶμεν» = A «For he suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved» and B «All of this he suffered for us, so that we might be saved». «ἀληθῶς ἔπαθεν, ὡς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν» keeps Christ as agent («raised himself») in both. «οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, αὐτοὶ το δοκεῖν ὄντες» is A «not as some unbelievers say, that he suffered in appearance, while they themselves exist in appearance» and B «No, it is they who are only an appearance», preserving the denial and the repeated τὸ δοκεῖν. «καθὼς φρονοῦσιν, καὶ συμβήσεται αὐτοῖς, οὖσιν ἀσωμάτοις καὶ δαιμονικοῖς» is the future befalling plus bodiless and demonic state in A «so it will also happen to them: they will be without bodies and like demons» and B «they will end up bodiless, like the demons». No scripture is quoted. Title names the thought. Accent notes on «δἰ» and «το δοκεῖν» are disclosed.

Pass A and Pass B both accurately reflect the Locked Greek: 'Ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα ἔπαθεν δἰ ἡμᾶς, ἵνα σωθῶμεν' rendered as 'All of this he suffered for us, so that we might be saved' (Pass B) and 'For he suffered all these things for our sake, so that we might be saved' (Pass A); 'καὶ ἀληθῶς ἔπαθεν, ὡς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν' as 'And he truly suffered, just as he also truly raised himself' (Pass A) and 'And he suffered truly, just as he truly raised himself' (Pass B); the reflexive 'ἀνέστησεν ἑαυτόν' correctly preserved as 'raised himself' in both; 'οὐχ ὥσπερ ἄπιστοί τινες λέγουσιν, τ� δοκεῖν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι' rendered as 'not as some unbelievers say, that he suffered in appearance' (Pass A) and 'Some unbelievers say his suffering was only an appearance' (Pass B); the Ignatian reversal 'αὐτοὶ τὸ δοκεῖν ὄντες' powerfully rendered as 'while they themselves exist in appearance' (Pass A) and 'No, it is they who are only an appearance!' (Pass B), matching the lemma choice rationale; 'καὶ καθὼς φρονοῦσιν, καὶ συμβήσεται αὐτοῖς' as 'And just as they think, so it will also happen to them' (Pass A) and 'And what they believe will become their lot' (Pass B); 'οὖσιν ἀσωμάτοις καὶ δαιμονικοῖς' as 'they will be without bodies and like demons' (Pass A) and 'they will end up bodiless, like the demons' (Pass B). All clauses present, no omissions, additions, or contradictions. Negation ('οὐχ'), agency (Christ as subject of suffering and raising; unbelievers as speakers; 'they' as subjects of thinking and being), modality (ἵνα σωθῶμεν purpose; καὶ συμβήσεται future), doctrine (affirmation of real suffering and resurrection against docetism; fate of unbelievers as bodiless and demon-like), and scripture (no inline citations, so vacuously satisfied) are preserved. Title 'He Truly Suffered; They Only Seem' captures the thought. Notes disclose OCR details: 'δἰ' and 'το δοκεῖν' without accent. No uncertainties. All source paragraph [1] covered.
